title: Archery Premier League Returns to Hyderabad as Asian Games Stars Turn Rivals
excerpt: Less than a week after India won nine Asian Games archery medals, the stars trade national jerseys for franchise rivalries in the Archery Premier League's second season, running October 8–18 in Hyderabad.
body:
• The Archery Premier League's second season runs October 8 to 18 at People's Plaza on Necklace Road, Hyderabad, with matches each evening from 7:30 to 9:30 PM IST.
  • 48 archers — 36 Indian and 12 international — will compete across six franchises in mixed-gender recurve and compound events, played with a 15-second shot clock.
  • India's Asian Games medallists return less than a week after Aichi-Nagoya as rivals: 17-year-old recurve gold medallist Kumkum Anil Mohod teams up with double gold winner Sahil Rajesh Jadhav at Chero Archers.
  • Tokyo Olympic champion Mete Gazoz, Brazil's Marcus D'Almeida and Britain's Ella Gibson headline the foreign field, alongside India's Deepika Kumari, Jyothi Surekha Vennam and Dhiraj Bommadevara.

From National Teammates to Franchise Rivals

Less than a week after returning from the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with nine archery medals, including five golds, India's archery stars will trade their national colors for franchise jerseys when the second season of the Archery Premier League (APL) begins in Hyderabad on October 8.

https://x.com/premierleague/status/2107184048242086129

The 11-day tournament at People's Plaza on Necklace Road brings together 48 archers across six franchises — Chero Archers (Jharkhand), Chola Chiefs (Tamil Nadu), Kakatiya Knights (Telangana), Mighty Marathas (Maharashtra), PrithviRaj Yodhas (Delhi) and defending champions Rajputana Royals (Rajasthan). The field is split equally between men and women, competing in both recurve and compound categories.

The teammates-to-rivals storyline is the season's central draw. The 17-year-old Kumkum Anil Mohod arrives in Hyderabad after making history at Aichi-Nagoya, where she became the first Indian to win an individual Asian Games gold in recurve archery. She will turn out for Chero Archers alongside Asian Games double gold medallist Sahil Rajesh Jadhav, Denmark's Mathias Fullerton and two-time Olympian Atanu Das. Chola Chiefs counter with Asian Games double gold winner Chikitha Taniparthi, Brazil's world-class Marcus D'Almeida, four-time Olympian Deepika Kumari and World Championships silver medallist Rajat Chauhan.

Context and Background

The league was initiated by the Archery Association of India (AAI) with the support of the Telangana government, and its inaugural edition — won by Rajputana Royals — drew strong digital engagement among younger audiences. Of this season's 48 archers, 21 return from the first season while 15 make their APL debut.

India's compound squad dominated the Asian Games, and the franchise rosters reflect that depth. Defending champions Rajputana Royals have built around Tokyo Olympic champion Mete Gazoz and British compound star Ella Gibson, backed by Asian Games gold medallist Ankita Bhakat, former world champion Ojas Pravin Deotale and Kushal Dalal. Mighty Marathas pair Asian Games silver medallist Dhiraj Bommadevara with Dutch compound great Mike Schloesser and Mexican Olympic medallist Alejandra Valencia. Kakatiya Knights are led by multiple Asian Games gold medallist Jyothi Surekha Vennam alongside Austria's Nico Wiener, Spain's Elia Canales and Asian Games silver medallist Neeraj Chauhan. Prithviraj Yodhas bank on Mexico's Andrea Becerra and former Asian Games gold medallist Abhishek Verma.

Impact and Analysis

The franchise format does something Indian archery rarely gets: regular, high-stakes competition against the world's best. National camps and World Cups are spaced out; a league compresses elite matchplay into 11 days, which matters most for the compound archers and the teenagers now on the radar for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic cycle.

For archers like Mohod and the 15 debutants, the APL is also a proving ground in front of a prime-time audience, with matches staged nightly in the 7:30–9:30 PM slot rather than morning qualifying rounds.

"India's Asian Games success gives the second season an exciting backdrop. Fans will now see those medallists compete across rival franchises, alongside some of the best archers in the world."

— Anil Kamineni, Director, Archery Premier League

"The league will help Indian archers to build on their international performances through regular competition with Olympic and World champions, while inspiring the next generation to take up the sport."

— Virender Sachdeva, Secretary General, Archery Association of India

Diaspora Angle

For Indian fans abroad, the APL is a new window into a sport that usually reaches them only through Olympic headlines. Names like Deepika Kumari and Atanu Das are familiar from four Olympic cycles; this season adds a debutante in Mohod who won Asian Games gold at 17. With Los Angeles 2028 on the horizon, the league gives the diaspora an early look at the archers India will field at the Games many of them will attend in person.

What's Next

Opening day is October 8, and the question is whether Rajputana Royals can defend their title against a field stacked with the archers who beat them at the Asian Games. The league runs through October 18, with results feeding into a domestic competition calendar that now looks more serious about keeping its stars sharp — and visible — between international assignments.
